questions.q: Which publisher is most likely EXCLUDED from the definition of investment adviser under the Uniform Securities Act?
options: A service that designs a portfolio for each subscriber after reviewing personal finances
A financial newsletter sold by subscription to the public that gives general market commentary, not advice tailored to individual subscribers
A website that charges each user for individual stock picks based on the user's tax situation
A planner who writes a personalized plan for each client
questions.explain: The publisher exclusion covers bona fide publications, in print or electronic form, that do not render advice based on the specific investment situation of each client. Once advice is personalized, the publisher is acting as an investment adviser.

questions.q: An SEC-registered investment adviser has a client in State Y. Which requirement may State Y impose on the firm?
options: A notice filing with copies of documents filed with the SEC, plus a fee
Full state registration and examination of the firm
State books-and-records requirements that exceed SEC rules
State minimum net worth requirements
questions.explain: Federal covered advisers are regulated by the SEC, but states may require notice filings, consent to service of process and fees, and may investigate and bring enforcement actions for fraud. They cannot require full registration of the firm or impose their own recordkeeping or capital requirements.

questions.q: An investment adviser with its principal office in a state that regulates advisers manages $105 million of client assets and does not advise any registered investment company. Under SEC rules, which statement is correct?
options: It must register with the SEC immediately
It may not register with the SEC under any circumstances
It must register with both the SEC and FINRA
It may register with the SEC but is not required to until assets reach $110 million
questions.explain: SEC Rule 203A-1 creates a buffer: an adviser with at least $100 million but less than $110 million under management may choose SEC registration. At $110 million or more it generally must register with the SEC, and an SEC-registered adviser need not withdraw unless assets fall below $90 million.

questions.q: A small investment adviser manages $30 million, but its only client is a mutual fund registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940. Where must it register?
options: With its home state only
With FINRA
With the SEC, regardless of its assets under management
Nowhere, because it has only one client
questions.explain: An adviser to a registered investment company is required to register with the SEC whatever its assets under management. The $100 million threshold applies to other advisers. Only one client does not create an exemption when that client is a registered fund.

questions.q: A state-regulated adviser with $60 million under management would have to register in 16 different states. Under the Investment Advisers Act, what option does it have?
options: It must register in all 16 states
It may register with the SEC instead, because it would otherwise have to register with 15 or more states
It may register only in its home state
It must reduce its client base
questions.explain: Mid-sized advisers are generally state-registered, but the Act lets an adviser register with the SEC if it would otherwise be required to register with 15 or more states. SEC Rule 203A-2 implements this multistate exemption, which also brings the firm under federal rules.

questions.q: An investment adviser registered in State A has no place of business in State B. In the past 12 months it has had four individual (non-institutional) clients residing in State B. Must it register in State B?
options: No, it falls within the de minimis exemption for advisers with no place of business in the state and no more than five such clients
Yes, any client in the state requires registration
Yes, because individuals are not institutional clients
No, but only if the clients are accredited investors
questions.explain: The Uniform Securities Act exempts an adviser with no place of business in the state that has had no more than five non-institutional clients there in the preceding twelve months. Federal law sets the same national de minimis standard (fewer than six clients). The adviser remains subject to the state's antifraud provisions.
questions.rule: Uniform Securities Act of 1956, Section 201(c); Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Section 222(d)

questions.q: An adviser acts solely as adviser to private funds and has $120 million of private fund assets under management in the U.S. Under the Investment Advisers Act, what is its status?
options: It must register with the SEC
It is unregulated and files nothing
It must register as a broker-dealer
It is exempt from SEC registration but must file reports with the SEC as an exempt reporting adviser
questions.explain: The private fund adviser exemption applies to advisers that advise only private funds and have less than $150 million of assets under management in the United States. These exempt reporting advisers still file portions of Form ADV with the SEC. States may separately regulate them.
questions.rule: Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Section 203(m); SEC Rule 204-4

questions.q: Which employee of a state-registered investment adviser is an investment adviser representative under the Uniform Securities Act?
options: A receptionist who schedules appointments
A clerk who processes paperwork without giving advice
An employee who solicits new clients for the firm's advisory services
An IT technician who maintains the firm's computers
questions.explain: An IAR is a partner, officer, director or other individual associated with an adviser who makes recommendations, manages accounts, determines advice to be given, solicits or negotiates the sale of advisory services, or supervises those who do. Clerical and support staff are not IARs.

questions.q: An IAR works for an SEC-registered (federal covered) adviser from an office in State Z. Under the Investment Advisers Act and the Uniform Securities Act, may State Z require her to register?
options: No, states have no authority over anyone associated with SEC-registered advisers
Yes, a state may register IARs of federal covered advisers who have a place of business in that state
Only if she has more than 100 clients
Only if she is also a broker-dealer agent
questions.explain: Federal law preempts state registration of SEC-registered firms but expressly preserves state authority to license or register IARs who have a place of business located in the state. The Uniform Securities Act therefore requires such IARs to register.

questions.q: An IAR leaves a state-registered investment adviser. Under the Uniform Securities Act, who must promptly notify the Administrator?
options: The investment adviser
Only the IAR
The SEC
The IAR's clients
questions.explain: When an IAR begins or ends employment with a state-registered adviser, the adviser must promptly notify the Administrator. If the employer is a federal covered adviser, the Act places the notice duty on the IAR. Clients and the SEC have no such filing obligation.

questions.q: Under the NASAA model rule on examination requirements, which qualification generally satisfies the exam requirement for an IAR?
options: Passing the Series 63 alone
Passing the Series 66 alone
Passing the Series 6 alone
Passing the Series 65, or passing the Series 66 together with the Series 7
questions.explain: IAR applicants generally must pass the Series 65, or the Series 66 combined with the Series 7. The Series 63 covers state law for agents only, and the Series 66 alone does not include the general securities knowledge tested on the Series 7. Some professional designations may qualify for a waiver.

questions.q: Under the Uniform Securities Act, when is an IAR's registration NOT effective?
options: During the month of December
During any period when the IAR has fewer than five clients
During any period when the IAR is not employed by an investment adviser registered under the Act
Whenever the IAR is on vacation
questions.explain: An IAR's state registration depends on employment with a registered adviser. If the IAR leaves and has not joined another registered adviser, the registration is not effective and the individual cannot act as an IAR until a new association is properly reported.

questions.q: Under SEC Rule 204-3, when must an SEC-registered adviser first deliver its Form ADV Part 2A brochure to a new client?
options: Within 90 days after the contract is signed
Before or at the time it enters into the advisory contract
Only if the client asks for it
At the end of the first year
questions.explain: The brochure must be delivered before or at the time the adviser enters into an advisory contract. Afterward, if there are material changes, the adviser must deliver an updated brochure or a summary of material changes each year within 120 days after its fiscal year end.

questions.q: Under SEC Rule 204-1, how often must an SEC-registered adviser file an updating amendment to Form ADV?
options: At least annually, within 90 days after the end of its fiscal year, and more often when certain information changes
Every five years
Only when it changes its name
Within 10 days after each new client
questions.explain: Advisers must file an annual updating amendment within 90 days of their fiscal year end. Form ADV instructions also require prompt amendments when certain items become inaccurate. State-registered advisers have parallel obligations under state rules.

questions.q: Under the Uniform Securities Act, which provision must an investment advisory contract contain?
options: That the adviser guarantees a minimum return
That the client waives the right to sue
That the adviser may raise fees without notice
That the adviser will not assign the contract without the client's consent
questions.explain: Advisory contracts must provide that the adviser will not be paid a share of capital gains (unless permitted by rule), that no assignment may be made without the client's consent, and that an adviser organized as a partnership will notify clients of membership changes. Guarantees and waivers are prohibited.

questions.q: Which advisory fee arrangement is permitted for any client under both the Uniform Securities Act and the Investment Advisers Act?
options: A fee equal to 20% of the account's capital gains, for a client with modest assets
A fee charged only when the account gains value, with no qualified-client status
A fee equal to a percentage of the account's total value measured at the end of each quarter
A share of the client's realized profits on each trade
questions.explain: Fees based on the total value of assets averaged over a period or measured on definite dates are not performance fees and are always allowed. Fees based on a share of capital gains or appreciation are generally prohibited unless the client meets the qualified-client standard or another exemption applies.
questions.rule: Investment Advisers Act of 1940, Section 205; Uniform Securities Act of 1956, Section 102(d)

questions.q: A state-registered adviser's advisory agreement authorizes it to have its fees deducted directly from client accounts held at a qualified custodian. For regulatory purposes, which statement is correct?
options: The adviser does not have custody because it never touches cash
The adviser is deemed to have custody and must follow the applicable custody safeguards
The arrangement is prohibited in all states
The adviser must become a bank
questions.explain: Authority to withdraw client funds, including fee deduction, is custody under the SEC and NASAA custody rules. Advisers relying on fee deduction must generally have written client authorization and follow the rules' notice and statement requirements, though some safeguards such as surprise exams may not apply to fee deduction alone.

questions.q: Under SEC Rule 206(4)-2, an adviser with custody of client assets generally must ensure which safeguards?
options: Assets are held by a qualified custodian that sends account statements at least quarterly, and an independent accountant performs a surprise examination at least once a year
The adviser holds client securities in its own office safe
Clients receive statements only on request
The adviser's own staff audits the accounts annually
questions.explain: The custody rule requires client funds and securities to be held by a qualified custodian such as a bank or broker-dealer, which sends statements at least quarterly, and generally requires an annual surprise examination by an independent public accountant at a time chosen by the accountant.

questions.q: A client mistakenly mails a stock certificate to her adviser instead of the custodian. Under the SEC custody rule, how can the adviser avoid having custody?
options: By holding it in a locked drawer for safekeeping
By depositing it into the adviser's own account
By keeping it until the next quarterly review
By returning it to the sender promptly, and in any case within three business days
questions.explain: Receiving client securities inadvertently does not create custody if the adviser returns them to the sender promptly, and in any case within three business days of receipt. Holding them longer, or depositing them, would bring the adviser under the custody requirements.

questions.q: An IAR receives oral discretionary authority from a client and places the first discretionary trade on Monday. Under the NASAA model rule on unethical adviser practices, by when must written discretionary authority be obtained?
options: Before the first trade, with no grace period
Within 30 calendar days after the first trade
Within 10 business days after the date of the first discretionary transaction
Never, if the client agreed orally
questions.explain: The NASAA rule treats exercising discretion as unethical unless written authority is obtained within ten business days after the first transaction placed under oral discretionary authority. Discretion limited to time or price of a specified trade is not covered. Broker-dealer agents, by contrast, need written authority before exercising discretion.
questions.rule: NASAA Model Rule 102(a)(4)-1, Unethical Business Practices of Investment Advisers

questions.q: Under the NASAA model rule on unethical business practices of investment advisers, from which client may an adviser borrow money?
options: Any client who agrees in writing
A client that is a financial institution in the business of lending money
Any client who has known the adviser for many years
Any client with a net worth over $1 million
questions.explain: Borrowing money or securities from a client is unethical unless the client is a broker-dealer, an affiliate of the adviser, or a financial institution engaged in lending. Written consent or a long relationship does not create an exception, because the conflict of interest remains.
questions.rule: NASAA Model Rule 102(a)(4)-1, Unethical Business Practices of Investment Advisers

questions.q: An adviser wants to sell a bond from its own inventory to an advisory client. Under the Uniform Securities Act, what must it do?
options: Disclose in writing that it is acting as principal and obtain the client's consent before the transaction is completed
Nothing, as long as the price is fair
Obtain the Administrator's approval in advance
Disclose its capacity within 30 days after settlement
questions.explain: An adviser acting as principal for its own account, or as broker for someone on the other side, must disclose its capacity in writing and obtain the client's consent before completion of the transaction. A fair price alone does not satisfy the requirement.

questions.q: Under SEC Rule 204A-1, when must an access person of an SEC-registered adviser submit an initial holdings report?
options: Within one year after becoming an access person
Only when buying an IPO
Never, if the person has no brokerage account
No later than 10 days after becoming an access person
questions.explain: The code of ethics rule requires access persons to report holdings within 10 days of becoming an access person and at least annually after that, and to file quarterly transaction reports within 30 days after each calendar quarter end. Access persons must also get pre-approval for IPO and limited offering purchases.

questions.q: An SEC-registered adviser's covered associate contributes $2,000 to the campaign of a city official who can influence the selection of advisers for the city pension plan. Under SEC Rule 206(4)-5, what is the consequence?
options: Nothing, because the contribution was personal
The adviser must refund the contribution within one year
The adviser is generally barred from receiving compensation for advising that government client for two years
The contribution is allowed if disclosed in Form ADV
questions.explain: The pay-to-play rule imposes a two-year time-out on compensated advisory business with a government entity after a covered contribution. Small contributions are excepted: up to $350 per election to an official the associate can vote for, or $150 otherwise. A $2,000 gift exceeds both limits.

questions.q: An adviser charges a client an advisory fee for a recommendation and its IAR also earns a commission when the client buys the recommended product through the IAR's broker-dealer. Under the NASAA model rule, what is required?
options: Nothing, because both fees are legal
Disclosing this conflict to the client in writing before advice is rendered
Refunding the commission to FINRA
Obtaining the Administrator's approval for each trade
questions.explain: The NASAA rule treats failing to disclose in writing, before advice is given, any material conflict of interest as unethical, specifically including charging an advisory fee when a commission on the resulting transaction will be received. Disclosure lets the client judge the advice.
questions.rule: NASAA Model Rule 102(a)(4)-1, Unethical Business Practices of Investment Advisers

questions.q: A broker-dealer detects a pattern of transactions totaling more than $5,000 that it suspects involves money laundering. Under FinCEN rules, by when must it generally file a Suspicious Activity Report?
options: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of the facts
Within one year
Only if the customer is convicted
Before telling the customer, within 24 hours
questions.explain: Broker-dealers must report suspicious transactions involving at least $5,000 within 30 calendar days of initial detection, with up to 30 more days allowed if no suspect has been identified (60 days at most). The firm may not tell the customer a SAR was filed. Large cash transactions above $10,000 are reported separately.

questions.q: An IAR tells a prospective client, 'Our firm is registered with the state, so the state has approved our investment strategy.' Under the Uniform Securities Act, this statement is:
options: Lawful, because the firm is registered
Lawful if the strategy has been profitable
Lawful if made orally
Unlawful, because registration does not mean the Administrator has passed on the merits of any person or strategy
questions.explain: The Act states that registration does not mean the Administrator has found any document true or has passed on the merits of, recommended or approved any person, security or transaction, and makes it unlawful to tell clients otherwise. Saying the firm is registered is fine; implying approval is not.
